According to reports, Apple will launch the next-generation Apple Silicon chip, the M6, later this year. This article compiles all currently known information, including why this generation will mark an unprecedented chapter in the Apple Silicon era.

M6 Specifications and Performance

According to a Bloomberg report, the Apple M6 chip will feature several major upgrades compared to the current M5.

First, the M6 chip will adopt an updated memory architecture, delivering faster memory bandwidth. Currently, the M5's memory bandwidth caps at 153 GB per second.

The M6 is reportedly set to boost memory bandwidth to 200 GB per second. Most notably, the higher memory bandwidth of the M6 will enhance on-device AI performance.

The M6 chip will also deliver comprehensive performance improvements across all cores and bring enhancements to video encoding and decoding.

Bloomberg also reports that the M6 chip will feature a redesigned GPU. Currently, the base-model M5 comes with up to 10 GPU cores, while the M6 is reportedly set to feature up to 12 graphics processing cores, meaning smoother gaming performance, faster video rendering, and better performance in GPU-accelerated applications.

Why the M6 Will Be Different

However, the M6 chip will differ from all previous Apple Silicon chips in one major respect.

Since the M1, Apple has consistently released higher-end "Pro" and "Max" variants, and even launched two "Ultra" chips during the M1, M2, and M3 eras.

But the M6 generation will break this convention. According to Mark Gurman, Apple will only release the base-model M6 processor, and will not launch any higher-end Pro, Max, or Ultra variants.

Apple reportedly believes that the improvements in the M7 are significant enough to skip most of the M6 product line. The M7 is reportedly set to bring larger upgrades in on-device AI processing, including support for memory bandwidth of up to 240 GB per second.

M6 Launch Date and Products

The M6 chip is reportedly set to debut as early as later this year. Apple has already been testing it on upgraded base-model MacBook Pro units equipped with the M5.

Whether the M6 chip will be used in other Apple products remains unknown. The base-model M7 is expected to launch in the first half of 2027, so most products will likely skip the M6 generation entirely.

What are your thoughts on Apple's upcoming M6 chip and strategic shift? Do you think this is the right decision? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
